1. Introduction
      Section 834 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY)
  2022 directs the Secretary of Defense (SecDef) to establish a competitive, merit-based pilot
  program to accelerate the procurement and fielding of innovative technologies (APFIT)
  (hereinafter “the APFIT pilot program” or “the pilot program”). Requirements for the pilot
  program include: establishing priority for Department of Defense (DoD) projects
  developed by small businesses and nontraditional defense contractors with $500,000,000
  or less in cumulative revenue from the DoD; collaborating with the Joint Staff and the
  Service Acquisition Executives (SAE); and project awards between $10 to $50 million.
  Additionally, the SecDef is required to collect data to assess the utility of this pilot program
  and biannual reports not later than March 1 and September 1 of each FY. Congress
  appropriated $100M in FY 2022 Procurement funds for the pilot program.
      The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering
  (OUSD(R&E)) manages the APFIT pilot program. In FY 2022 the OUSD(R&E), in
  collaboration with the Military Services, DoD Agencies, the Joint Staff, and the Office of
  the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSD(A&S)), executed
  a merit-based internal DoD solicitation, evaluation, and selection process. Ten projects
  were selected for funding, to receive $10 million. The FY 2023 solicitation, evaluation,
  and selection process for the APFIT pilot program is currently underway.

2. Participants
      In FY 2022 the APFIT pilot program focused on engaging with the Military Services
  and DoD Agencies through their lead Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and
  Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program offices to solicit and nominate
  projects for APFIT funding. The specific Military Services and DoD Agencies that
  participated in the APFIT pilot program in FY 2022 were:
     -   Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
     -   Defense Health Agency
     -   Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)
     -   Defense Logistics Agency
     -   Defense Microelectronics Activity
     -   Defense Threat Reduction Agency
     -   Missile Defense Agency (MDA)
     -   National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency
     -   Strategic Capabilities Office
     -   Space Development Agency (SDA)*
     -   U.S. Air Force (USAF)
     -   U.S. Army (USA)
     -   U.S. Marine Corps (USMC)
     -   U.S. Navy (USN)

        *Note: Effective October 1, 2022, the SDA was transferred to the USSF and is no longer

        previously have been under the purview of the SDA.

    3. FY 2022 Selected Projects

          The following 10 projects were selected in FY 2022 to receive $10M of FY 2022
        APFIT funding. 1
        1. Advanced Sensor Package Procurement
              a. Project Description: Accelerates procurement of a multi-sensor payload for use
                 in unmanned underwater vehicles that will enable safe passage of U.S. and
                 allied naval forces with advanced mine-hunting capabilities
              b. Company: Arete Associates
              c. Contract Award Date: August 22, 2022
              d. Production Quantities: Six small synthetic aperture module (SSAM) sonars and
                 18 video automatic target recognition (VATR) common module (VCM) kits
              e. Delivery Start Date: November 1, 2023 (VCM); August 1, 2024 (SSAM)
              f. Delivery End Date: September 30, 2025
              g. Delivery Rate: Eight units per month (VCM); Two units every four months
                 (SSAM);
              h. Estimated Amount of Time that APFIT Funding Accelerated the DoD
                 Capability: 24 months

        2. Anti-Jam Radio-links for Maritime Operations Resiliency (ARMOR)
              a. Project Description: Initial procurement of small antennas for resilient
                  communications that conform to platform outer mold lines. Procure and certify
                  a standalone ARMOR platform agnostic package for scalability across multi-
                  domain platforms and two pre-low rate of initial production (LRIP) network
                  certified ARMOR units ready for platform integration. Provides high data rate
                  capacity scalable to support multi-mission needs and connects the national
                  technical means to the tactical edge
              b. Company: Pacific Antenna Systems, Titan Systems LLC, and Naval Systems,
                  Inc.
              c. Contract Award Date: November 11, 2022
